title: Customer recovery decision cookbook and closure note (draft)
body:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working draft for (1) short statuspage snippets at each phase of a multi-wave inference outage, (2) a concise customer-facing post-incident summary, and (3) a decision cookbook that helps customers choose between automatic recovery, manual replay, or requesting a replay package. Primary audience: customers impacted by request-level integrity issues and internal CS/Support leads drafting outbound messages.

High-level summary (one-sentence, for headline use):
We experienced a regional inference processing regression that caused delayed and occasionally duplicated/partial responses for a subset of requests; services have been restored and we are offering targeted recovery/replay options for impacted tenants.

Suggested statuspage/ops snippets (copy-paste friendly)
1) Initial detection (short):
  - Title: Investigating increased partial/duplicated responses in EU inference region
  - Body: We are investigating reports of delayed, truncated, and in a small percentage of cases duplicated responses from the EU inference region. Our telemetry shows an uptick starting ~2026-10-09T22:30Z. Engineers are actively triaging. If you are seeing missing tokens or duplicate chunks, please open a support ticket and include request IDs if available.

2) Progress update (mid-incident):
  - Title: Mitigation underway — routing and rate adjustments applied
  - Body: We have deployed temporary routing changes and adjusted tenant-level throttles to limit exposure while we validate kernel/queueing fixes. The majority of requests are now flowing through fallback capacity; some customers may still see delayed responses. We are continuing validation and will provide a resolution ETA within 2 hours.

3) Resolution/closure (customer-facing):
  - Title: Incident resolved — service restored, recovery options available
  - Body: Root cause has been identified and mitigations applied. All production routing paths are restored. If you observed truncated, duplicated, or otherwise incorrect responses between 2026-10-09T22:30Z and 2026-10-10T05:12Z, please review the recovery options below to choose how you want affected requests handled.

Customer-facing post-incident summary (concise, plain language)
Impact
  - What happened: A queuing regression combined with a selective kernel-level timeout caused some in-flight responses to be returned incomplete or duplicated for a subset of tenants in the EU region.
  - Who was affected: Approximately 0.6% of requests for tenants routed to EU high-throughput pools during the window. Affected response types: streaming generation and structured outputs with KV-cache lengths > 2k tokens.
  - Service effect: Increased latency for affected requests, occasional truncated outputs and rare duplicate segments. No customer data was exfiltrated.

Root cause (non-sensitive summary)
  - The regression was triggered during a rolling optimization that changed kernel selection logic for long-context sequences; an interaction between the new selector and the queue backpressure calculation allowed some requests to exit the critical path prematurely, producing partial writes to streaming buffers.
  - Why it wasn't caught earlier: The change only impacts uncommon long-KV-cache sequences and our smoke tests did not include sufficient long-context streaming scenarios.

Immediate remediation and mitigations applied
  - Reverted the kernel-selector change and deployed a hotfix to the queue backpressure logic (INF-4721).
  - Applied conservative routing to fallback pools for at-risk tenants while validation completed.
  - Added additional telemetry for long-context streaming latencies and buffer-commit confirmations.

Permanent actions (follow-ups)
  - Expand smoke tests to include long-KV-cache streaming generation (owner: eng-serving-runtime, ETA: 2026-11-01).
  - Add an automated regression check that simulates mid-stream buffer preemption (owner: release-engineering, ETA: 2026-11-08).
  - Review and tighten rollout flags for kernel-selector changes (owner: platform-engineering, ETA: 2026-10-25).

Customer recovery options (decision cookbook)
Context: We detect which requests likely produced invalid outputs and can offer three recovery paths. Choose one per-tenant or per-route depending on customer needs.
Option A — Auto-replay (recommended for most customers)
  - What we do: Redwood will automatically re-run (replay) affected requests against the restored runtime, preserving original request inputs and model pins. Replays are run with priority and do not count against normal per-tenant quotas; we cap replays to requests within the incident window and to identified impacted request IDs.
  - Pros: Fast, minimal customer effort, preserves request fidelity.
  - Cons: Small chance of non-deterministic outputs for non-deterministic sampling models (we provide both original and replayed output for audit).
  - Suggested customer public messaging: "Redwood has reprocessed requests that may have been affected. Please review replayed outputs and contact Support for any discrepancies."

Option B — Replay package (for audit / compliance)
  - What we do: Provide a downloadable package with request inputs, timestamps, and logs so customers can re-run locally or in a private environment. We can also provide a replay runner suggestion (example script).
  - Pros: Full auditability, useful for regulated workflows.
  - Cons: Requires customer effort to re-run.
  - Suggested messaging: "We’ve prepared a replay package with inputs and evidence for your internal audit team. Contact Support to request the package."

Option C — No action / manual handle
  - Customers may opt to handle affected requests internally (e.g., drop, flag, or manual reprocess). We will provide a CSV of impacted request IDs.
  - Pros: Maximum customer control.
  - Cons: Manual work required.

How to choose (quick decision tree)
  - If you need minimal effort and want Redwood to ensure replayed outputs are available: choose Auto-replay (A).
  - If you require an auditable package for compliance teams: choose Replay package (B).
  - If you already have internal replay / ingestion pipelines and prefer to reprocess yourself: choose No action (C).

Operational details for the Auto-replay (A)
  - Scope: We will target request IDs where we have high-confidence evidence of partial/duplicate output (matching buffer-commit anomalies + request timing).
  - Timeline: Replays begin within 24 hours after customer opt-in; expected completion within 72 hours for most tenants. Large tenants may take longer and will be contacted with a timeline.
  - Output delivery: Replayed outputs will be placed into the tenant’s storage bucket (path: redwood-replays/<tenant-id>/2026-10-10/) and a ticket will be opened with links to the artifacts.
  - Quotas/cost: No charge for compute replay during this incident; log/transfer storage handled per standard billing.

Suggested email / support template (for CS reps)
  - Subject: Redwood incident recovery options for [Tenant name] — action required
  - Body: Hi [Name], we’ve completed remediation for the EU inference incident that may have affected some of your requests between 2026-10-09T22:30Z and 2026-10-10T05:12Z. We can (A) auto-replay affected requests on your behalf, (B) provide a replay package for your team, or (C) share a CSV of impacted request IDs if you'd like to reprocess internally. Please reply with A/B/C and any constraints (e.g., PCI/PHI handling). Regards, Asha (Customer Success).

FAQ (short)
  - Q: Will replays produce identical outputs?
    A: If your endpoint uses deterministic decoding (e.g., greedy), outputs will match. For sampling-based decoding (temperature, top-k/top-p), replayed outputs may differ; we retain original outputs alongside replays for comparison.
  - Q: Is there any data loss?
    A: No. Input payloads are preserved and we have the request traces. We found no evidence of data exfiltration.
  - Q: Will this affect my billing?
    A: Redwood will not charge for the compute used for incident replays. Standard storage/transfer fees apply.

Customer communication variants (tone and length)
  - Brief (status-page / tweet-length): "Resolved: EU inference regional issue affecting long-context streaming. Recovery options available — contact support to opt-in."
  - Detailed (enterprise email): Use the template above and include link to the full post-incident summary and replay options.

Draft closure note (for customers after they choose an option and replays complete)
  - Title: Closure: Replays completed for affected requests
  - Body: We’ve completed replaying confirmed affected requests for [Tenant]. Replays are available at: <link>. We’ve also included the original outputs for your audit. If you detect any unexpected differences, please escalate to your account team and we will prioritize review and remediation.

Open questions / TODOs (internal)
  - [ ] Confirm exact storage path naming convention for replay artifacts and include example URLs (action: eng infra).
  - [ ] Validate privacy constraints for replay package export (PII/PHI) and add approval checklist for opt-in (action: security/compliance).
  - [ ] Decide policy for customers on whether replays should be automatically applied for tenants with SLA credits over X (action: CS policy).
  - [ ] Draft a short KB article explaining deterministic vs non-deterministic model replays and how to interpret differences (action: developer-experience).

Notes to self / internal phrasing to avoid in customer comms
  - Avoid deep kernel/selector implementation details.
  - Do not publish low-level commit ids or internal rollout flags.
  - Keep technical appendix high-level and put sensitive artefacts behind enterprise support ticket.

Appendix (evidence excerpts, internal only)
  - Timeline: 2026-10-09T22:29Z — first anomaly metric spike; 22:30Z — customer reports begin; 22:55Z — temporary routing applied; 23:42Z — kernel-selector rollback initiated; 00:18Z — queue backpressure hotfix deployed; 05:12Z — all routes restored and validation green.
  - Related tickets: INF-4721 (primary fix), INF-4729 (telemetry expansion).
  - Slack threads: #inc-aws-eu (triage thread), #cs-ops (customer coordination).

Draft sign-off checklist for sending final closure message to customers
  - Confirm replays completed or CSV/package ready
  - Security sign-off for package contents if requested
  - Confirm billing treatment for the tenant (waivers for compute)
  - Include link to post-incident summary and list of follow-up actions with ETA

End of draft.
_notes: working doc; put final closure note into support ticket templates and publish a KB article after engineering follow-up actions complete
